en: The *Cintāmaṇicakravarti-guhyasākṣāt-buddhatva-siddhi-suvarṇacakravarti-mantrarāja-sūtra*,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Da Guangzhi of Daxingshan Monastery.
Translated by Amoghavajra by Imperial Decree. Chapter One: The Releasing of the Alms Bowl. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavat was on the summit of the Great Snow Mountains, within the Prajñā-kūṭa of Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
He was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
all of whom were great arhats,
as well as immeasurable and innumerable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Namely: the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha.

Together with such great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, as well as the eighteen Vajras, the twelve Great Devas, and immeasurable hosts of the eight classes of benevolent spirit-kings and their countless retinues.
They surrounded him from the front and the rear. At that time, within the assembly,
there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Mañjuśrī.
Possessing profound and weighty great compassion and immeasurable wisdom,
he was the foremost among all bodhisattvas;
rising from his seat, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain for the great assembly the merit of setting aside the alms bowl.
This great assembly wishes to hear it and practice accordingly.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī!
You all should listen attentively and reflect upon this well.
I shall now [speak] here in this great assembly for the sake of all eight classes of beings and for future generations.
For the sake of those who practice the secret and wholesome Dharma, as well as the seers, sages, and noble ones who perform difficult and arduous ascetic practices,
he taught the essential method for setting aside the alms bowl.
At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
"So be it, World-Honored One; we wish and desire to hear it.
The Buddha addressed the youth Mañjuśrī, saying:
"If there are sons or daughters of good family who wish to fly through the air with their alms-bowls while practicing the holy path of the Buddhas to benefit sentient beings..."
First, select high mountains and deep valleys;
whether they resemble an overturned bowl or an upturned bowl,
they should be secluded and devoid of people— such is the most excellent environment.
He constructed a hermitage solely for the purpose of dwelling alone in this pure place of practice;
he ceased speech and remained silent, abandoned the five grains,
and subsisted on pine needles, swallowing water and inhaling air.
Practice meditative concentration and silent reflection;
recite the dhāraṇī of the Eight Great Dragon Kings and their names without allowing for any other distractions.
When three hundred days have passed, take one *hu* of non-glutinous rice.
Dry it for one hundred days.
Being able to maintain the fasts and precepts without violating the rules of decorum,
single-mindedly recite the name of the Buddha Ratnasaṃbhava.
Next, recite the name of the Buddha Prabhūtaratna.
Then, taking an empty bowl, invoke all the dragon kings (*nāgarāja*) and the garuḍa bird kings,
reciting the mantra ten thousand three hundred times for each.
Sinking into the midst of space, a great wind-wheel arose;
at that time, the King of the Garuḍas and the Great Nāga King Sāgara and others mounted that wind-wheel,
carrying an empty bowl upon its summit.
He reaches the palaces of the various nāga kings and the palaces of the asuras in the heavens,
where he immediately takes long-life elixirs of the immortals and bestows them upon the practitioner.
Having consumed them, the practitioner lives for a thousand years with supernormal powers at will.
One who is capable of practicing the path of the Buddha’s sublime Dharma may approach women or eat meat; however, such a person shall not be able to fly their alms bowl,
and their supernormal powers will be suddenly brought to a halt.
This is the essential method of practice and secret dharma of the divine immortals of former Buddhas.
I now proclaim this essential teaching for you and for sentient beings of future ages who lack merit.
"Mañjuśrī, you must uphold this essential teaching and proclaim it for the sake of sentient beings during the final dharma period after my parinirvāṇa."
By this cause, one attains liberation from the ocean of suffering of birth and death. Mañjuśrī said:
"We, this great assembly, have obtained a great benefit."
"We shall uphold this secret dharma to benefit sentient beings, causing all *siddhis* to be fully realized.
**Chapter Two: On the Causes and Effects of Good and Evil** At that time, there was a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva within the assembly.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, named Amoghapāśarāja, rose from his seat,
bared his right shoulder, joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"So be it, World-Honored One!
Now this great assembly, having heard the Dharma of the Empty Bowl, the Great Fulfillment, and the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels,
shall forever weary of human society and set their hearts on delighting in mountain forests."
Not accepting offerings of faith while desiring to practice the Buddha-way—
this Dharma is subtle and wondrous, serving as a great skillful means to benefit sentient beings;
it is the wish-fulfilling jewel for the practitioner.
However, in the final age when the Dharma is about to perish,
sentient beings will lack merit and their faculties of faith will be shallow;
they will be incapable of practicing the path and teachings of the Buddhas.
In this way, sentient beings who commit much evil and frequently fall into the evil destinies have no prospect of escape;
all this is due to the karma of great stinginess and greed in previous lives.
The obstacles in both worlds are entirely caused by the karma of poverty and the lack of merit and wisdom. It is thus.
For those sentient beings of the final age who practice the secret dharma with the aspiration for the fruit of Buddhahood,
the Bhagavān has taught the Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Wheel of Merit and Wisdom activities.
This skillful means of the Ratnakula has never before been taught as a wheel of Dharma by the Buddhas.
Now, in this assembly, I shall turn this wheel of Dharma for the benefit of sentient beings.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Amogharāja, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Avalokiteśvara!"
Since beginningless time, you have cultivated the samādhis of great loving-kindness and great compassion throughout the great kalpas;
you have thereby attained the body of the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels, the Samādhi of Universally Manifesting Form-Bodies.
Now, for this inquiry, I request that you explain the essential points of the Dharma of Great Compassion.
Listen attentively and reflect upon it well.
I shall now explain for you the matters of the causes and effects of karma regarding poverty and merit.
If sentient beings possess the nature of wisdom yet lack the retribution of merit,
they consequently commit offenses and fall into the various evil realms;
such persons frequently give rise to great stinginess and greed.
Because they practiced *prajñā*, they possess wisdom in this present life but are poor in merit.
If there are sentient beings who possess merit but lack wisdom,
these individuals extensively practiced giving in previous lives.
Because they do not cultivate meditative concentration, they possess merit in this life but lack wisdom.
Such karmic retributions vary in many ways;
thus, fixed karma is difficult to alter.
Because cause and effect are fixed,
it is difficult to alter [karmic destiny]. Therefore, the Buddhas possess various skillful means and secret,
wondrous arts that can transform the power of the fixed karmic retribution of sentient beings, enabling them to obtain merit and long life.
The dharma of the Great Siddhi of All Auspiciousness shall be definitively accomplished.
You shall obtain it within a mere moment.
There is a great Nāga King who presides over it.
It is named "Able to Accomplish All the Wishes and Desires of Sentient Beings.
Not far from here is a great lake,
pure and stainless, where no predatory birds dwell.
The four shores are composed of the four precious substances—
gold, silver, lapis lazuli, musaragalva, crystal, and pearl— and are extensively adorned with immeasurable ornaments.
In their midst sits a great nāga king within a copper-precious palace supported by five pillars.
He is named the Nāga King Anavatapta;
he is capable of accomplishing all karmas, abides in the eighth stage, the Samādhi of Immovability,
and possesses compassion for all sentient beings.
There is always the nectar-like water of wisdom and Dharma that nurtures the five grains and causes all things to grow;
because of this, the human and dharmic laws suffer no deficiency.
I have now traveled to the palace of the Great Nāga King at the Pond of Prajñā.
I wish to expound the Dharma of the Great Bodhisattva Cintāmaṇi-ratna.
You, the great assembly, should hold it for a short while;
at that time, there will surely be realization.
At that time, there were the Great Bodhisattvas such as the Great Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel,
the Great Dharma Prince Vajrapāṇi,
and the assembly of Great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas in the stage of great consecration.
The entire assembly remained silent, awaiting the opportune moment.
Chapter Three: The Wish-Fulfilling Jewel. At that time, the Dragon King of the Lake Anavatapta—
Emerging spontaneously from the Copper-Wheel Dragon Palace at Lake Anavatapta,
he proceeded to the place where Śākyamuni Buddha was.
Descending from a purple cloud, he prostrated before the World-Honored One and made offerings with deep reverence.
Together with his retinue, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, we pray that you will enter my palace and accept my offerings.
The sentient beings within the pond desire to hear the profound and wondrous Dharma."
"We only pray that the Tathāgata, out of great compassion, will graciously accept our invitation.
For this reason, we and our retinues have come to offer this request.
At that time, the World-Honored One accepted the dragon king's invitation.
Immediately, the precious throne rose up, emitting a great radiance that illuminated the ten directions.
All Buddha-worlds, which eternally abide within the Dharma-realm,
and the pure jewel-lands shook in six ways.
Heavenly jeweled flowers fell in profusion,
like winter rain, and also like a flight of birds.
At that time, the World-Honored Buddhas of the ten directions,
the assembly of great bodhisattvas, and all the eight classes of beings who possessed supernatural powers—
All of them came and gathered together like clouds at once.
At that time, the World-Honored One, together with the great assembly,
all walked through the great void of space.
Riding upon yellow clouds onto a white lotus pedestal,
he performed celestial music as he entered the palace of the Dragon King;
the great assembly of the eight classes of beings also followed behind the Buddha.
Each manifested their own supernatural powers.
At that time, the palace of the Great Nāga King Anavatapta trembled in six ways;
precious lotus flowers rained down, and celestial drums resounded of their own accord.
A brilliant light shone forth.
At that time, the dragon sons and dragon daughters within the pond,
together with their great retinues, all assembled there at once.
They adorned the precious hall, prepared the lion throne,
and arranged the offerings to welcome the Tathāgata.
At that time, the World-Honored One, by means of his supernormal powers,
entered the dragon palace and took his place upon a precious lion throne. That throne was adorned with moonlight-mani jewels, crystal, white silver, and exquisite *ratna* gems.
That palace was a precious palace with five pillars of red copper;
on its left and right were five thousand pavilions each,
and within that palace there were various jewel trees.
Everywhere there are jewel ponds, jewel pools, jewel mountains, and jewel peaks, as well as jewel birds—
namely peacocks, parrots, and jīvañjīvaka birds— all singing harmoniously and sporting together.
At that time, the Tathāgata sat upon a jeweled throne like a mountain of gold;
receiving their offerings,
he proclaimed the essential points of the Dharma for the great dragon kings.
The details of this matter are fully recounted in the *Anavatapta-nāgarāja-sūtra*.
At that time, there was a nāga girl within the assembly whose appearance was wondrous and exquisite like that of a celestial maiden, and whose mind was harmonious and refined.
At that time, a great bodhisattva named Shan-nü (Good Woman) rose from her seat,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: "In our previous lives, our karmic obstacles were profound and heavy."
Because you harbored greed, hatred, and delusion, and failed to plant the seeds of wisdom,
I have now been born within the waters of this lake in the form of a woman;
though I am free from burning afflictions and all manner of suffering, I still dwell among the scales of the animal realm.
May I, in birth after birth, never again receive a female body nor perform the deeds of a woman.
Through the power of making offerings to the Buddha and hearing the Dharma,
may I dedicate all these merits toward the subtle and wondrous path of the Buddha.
Seeking no other fruit, she aspired solely to attain Buddhahood.
At that time, the Dragon King’s Daughter immediately praised the Buddha before him with these verses:
The World-Honored One’s countenance is like the moonlight; pure, exquisite, and beyond compare.
Today we take refuge, having heard the Dharma through the profound depth of our past merits;
that we have attained the Way is not in vain. I possess a precious jewel.
I offer this to the World-Honored One for the benefit of sentient beings,
so that they may obtain the jewel of the Dharma and repay the Buddha’s kindness; to protect the Secret Teachings,
to lead all equally to the fruit of Buddhahood, to expound the Three Vehicles, and to benefit all.
At that time, after the Dragon King’s daughter, the virtuous woman, had spoken these verses,
she took a precious jewel and offered it to the Tathāgata,
saying these words:
I only pray that the World-Honored One will accept this precious jewel from me.
This is a wish-fulfilling jewel,
which lies within a crystal jeweled casket at the bottom of the Dragon Abyss, nine layers deep within the azure ocean.
The father king kept it secret, and the various nāgas guarded, revered,
and honored it as if it were Śakra’s precious jar of nectar,
which fulfills all wishes.
If sentient beings obtain this precious jewel,
all their actions and all their aspirations will be fulfilled according to their wishes and intentions; all siddhis shall be accomplished.
Because I now value the Dharma more than material wealth,
I offer this to the World-Honored One, whose price is beyond measure.
I only pray that the Hero of the World will graciously accept it.
The Buddha said to the dragon girl:
"Now you wish to offer this precious jewel for the sake of protecting the True Dharma;
I accept this pure and white jewel of your faithful mind."
He did not accept the exquisite dragon-jewel. Why was this?
Because the wish-fulfilling jewel—
It is neither possessing jewels nor lacking jewels;
it is neither sentient nor non-sentient;
it is neither stone nor gold.
The perfection of giving (dānapāramitā) arises spontaneously.
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas possess four kinds of precious jewels, namely:
the jewels of loving-kindness (maitrī), compassion (karuṇā), sympathetic joy (muditā), and equanimity (upekṣā).
By bestowing [this] upon all sentient beings within the twenty-five realms of existence,
there is then a vajra-jewel banner within the ocean of the Dharma-realm;
it is topped with this precious gem.
I constantly and universally rain down the precious wealth of the merits of ethical discipline, meditative concentration,
and wisdom for the sake of all sentient beings,
so that they may attain fulfillment in the six pāramitās, ascend the ladder of the ten bhūmis, and master the eighty thousand dharma-treasuries.
Although the Dragon Palaces of the human realm are situated within its immediate vicinity, the karmic fruits of their water and land are nonetheless distinct;
thus, the human realm also possesses wish-fulfilling jewels (*cintāmaṇi*).
Among these, the jewel of the ten wholesome deeds belonging to a Wheel-Turning Sage King (*cakravartin*) is the most supreme.
Regarding the eight precepts and five precepts of medium and lower grades,
although the people may have merely heard their names, they do not grasp their essential substance.
If there is a wise person who receives and upholds these categories of precepts, the legal codes, and the ritual protocols, [they shall attain the fruit].
For the sake of protecting the True Dharma and benefiting humans and devas,
one who seeks the Dharma-treasure shall also obtain the Cintāmaṇi jewel.
This jewel is a great secret wish-fulfilling jewel fashioned among humanity.
Furthermore, these are not the precious jewels belonging to the Dragon Palace.
Dragons possess the virtue of water,
while humans possess the virtue of fire.
Because it is a precious jewel that manifests through the differentiation of yin and yang,
it is also not the same as the bright pearl in the ocean that becomes a wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi) for those who obtain it.
Since this matter is so rare, it is considered a mere fabrication; therefore, I do not accept your wish-fulfilling jewel.
You must protect my True Dharma and all sentient beings of future ages, ensuring they do not lose mindfulness.
"This is a pearl; this is a precious gem.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this Dharma-gate, [remained silent].
Upon hearing this profound Dharma, the dragon girl wept with deep sorrow;
prostrating herself with her five limbs touching the ground, she addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One!"
"I would rather lose my life than dare to disobey the Buddha’s command.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha...
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha,
together with his retinue of five hundred jewel divisions,
rose from his seat and addressed the Buddha, saying:
I pray that the Buddha will expound the Dharma of the wish-fulfilling jewel,
so as to eliminate the poverty and suffering of sentient beings who lack merit,
and to enable them to attain the supreme, wondrous, and unsurpassed great fruit of merit, wisdom, and auspiciousness.
The Buddha addressed the two great beings, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
You should receive and uphold these words of the Buddha, and do not let them be forgotten or lost."
I now wish to expound this most profound Dharma, the secret treasury of all Buddhas;
this Dharma is the noble eye of all Bodhisattvas.
This dharma is the embodiment of the Vairocana flower pedestal;
this dharma is the Vairocana vajra-summit jewel;
this dharma is the supreme, most honored, subtle, and profoundly deep great consecration jewel upon the crowns of all meritorious qualities.
I shall now proclaim it;
you should receive and uphold it, and reflect upon it well for the benefit of the world.
I now address you, great beings of profound rank whose past merit is deep and vast.
This cannot be known by ordinary persons of the stage of thinning [defilements].
If there are sentient beings who desire the merit, longevity, and wish-fulfilling jewels of the dragon palaces within the heavens,
they should first receive the empowerment ritual from a Great Ācārya.
Having entered the great maṇḍala of the Buddha’s realm,
they receive and accept with profound resolve the great adamantine aspiration;
they immediately receive and accept the great samaya precepts in person, never transgressing the majestic deportment.
For the sake of benefiting sentient beings and protecting the True Dharma, he fashioned a precious jewel.
Furthermore, he synthesized an *cintāmaṇi* (wish-fulfilling jewel) from eleven kinds of rare treasures.
These were as follows: the first was the relics of the Buddha.
Second, gold; third, silver; fourth, agarwood.
Fifth, white sandalwood;
sixth, red sandalwood;
seventh, fragrant peach wood.
Eighth, *sānta* aloeswood;
ninth, *śvetacitta* tree aloeswood;
tenth, cypress aloeswood.
Eleventh is genuine lacquer.
Within this, a globular form fashioned from gold and silver serves as an *cintāmaṇi* jewel;
inside it, thirty-two grains of the Buddha’s *śarīra* are enshrined.
Having applied fragrant powder and clay to the surface of the precious vessel and fashioned the precious jewel,
he then took a nine-striped saffron-colored *kāṣāya* robe.
This profound and esoteric [teaching] enters eighteen layers of the pure Brahma-casket.
Each layer represents the nine mountains and eight seas,
augmented by the Great Iron Ring Mountains.
Finally, the four precious colors of the Brahma-casket were formed:
the first was the color of tempered steel;
the middle was golden; and the others were red and white silver.
Each of the eight layers was completely sealed so that non-humans,
petty people, and even the celestial Māras could not see them.
Once the construction was finished.
Establishing the maṇḍala and preparing incense and flowers,
one should pay homage with reverence;
thus one will certainly achieve great siddhi.
Do not harbor doubts; practice and recite with earnest devotion day and night.
This is the secret, great wish-fulfilling jewel of human diligence, surpassing even the precious gems and jewels found in the palaces of the nāgas.
This is the most supreme jewel among men.
If there are no physical relics (śarīra), one should fashion them from gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, agate, pearl, and various other precious gems.
The jewels are used as described above.
For a practitioner who lacks the power [to obtain them],
one may go to the shore of the great ocean and collect pure sand or pebbles to serve as śarīra.
Furthermore, medicinal herbs, bamboo, wood, roots, and nodes were fashioned into śarīras,
numbering thirty-two grains in total,
seven of which served as the primary ones.
Measuring about the size of a chicken egg,
he immediately fashioned a precious jewel.
That jewel emitted light that universally illuminated all who were poor, destitute, and suffering.
"Just as your precious jewel has no distinction [from others]," the Buddha said to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi,
"if there is a practitioner of yoga who desires to fulfill their heart's wish..."
The Ritual for Establishing the Maṇḍala Altar:
Facing the Bodhisattva Śāri-king-ratna, one prays and makes vows;
that which is sought shall emerge as subtle and wondrous speech from within one’s own jewel.
"Whatever aspiration you seek, I shall now fulfill it.
At that time, the practitioner reveals their heart's desire,
whether it be mundane or supramundane.
May all aspirations for long life and merit be fulfilled;
may all people hold one in affection and respect, and may evil persons be subdued.
May the elixir of longevity be attained, and may one enter caves in meditative concentration, possessing the supernormal power of flight.
This shall fulfill the heart's aspirations sought in this present life:
the perfection of the six pāramitās, the transcendental realization of the ten bhūmis,
the seven stages of equal enlightenment, and the dharma of the eightfold noble path.
The four immeasurable minds and such dharmas as these are called supramundane dharmas.
All matters that one contemplates will certainly be accomplished.
Chapter Four: The Great Maṇḍala. The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, saying:
"If a practitioner who maintains the recitation wishes to construct a maṇḍala to achieve great siddhi..."
Mix cow dung with yellow earth to form a paste,
and apply it as an ointment according to the ritual rules. Then, [apply] white sandalwood, spikenard, saffron, camphor, and musk.
Having smeared, purified, and adorned the altar,
place the sovereign wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi-rāja) upon it;
in the center, place the Great Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
Directly behind, one installs the Bodhisattva Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
To the right, one installs the Bodhisattvas Amoghapāśa-Lokeśvara, Gaganagañja, Kṣitigarbha, Maitreya, and so forth.
In front on the left, one should install Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, Sūryaprabha Bodhisattva, and Candraprabha Bodhisattva.
In the lower part of the front left, one should install Acala Dūtaka.
To the right of the aforementioned lower section are installed the Vajra-Muṇḍarī, the Bodhisattva Jalaśrī, the Bodhisattva Amoghapāśa Avalokiteśvara, as well as the One-Tufted Rākṣasa Messenger,

Brahmā, Śakra Devendra, the Four Great Heavenly Kings, Īśvara, Maheśvara, Yama, Pṛthivī, Nārāyaṇa, Sarasvatī, Śrīdevī, the Vidyādharas, the Dragon Kings and Dragon Queens, Hārītī, the Deity of Crops, and others.
On both sides, arrange five-colored powders in parallel lines;
let the powders form a horizontal outer boundary.
Set out one hundred and sixty-four lamps, oil, *argha* offerings, incense, and flowers.
Prepare various offerings of food and drink according to the Dharma, ensuring they are provided without interruption.
Every day, observe the eightfold precepts of the fast and resolve for bodhicitta.
By constructing this maṇḍala,
all siddhis will certainly be accomplished.
The Buddha also declared:
I shall now again explain the method for painting the maṇḍala of the image.
First, paint the great ocean.
Within that great ocean, also paint a great jewel palace with two tiers.
It was adorned with immeasurable precious jewels.
Within that palace, a mandala of the seven treasures was painted;
upon a precious lotus flower, the king of wish-fulfilling jewels was depicted.
Then, one should cause a fire-light to emanate.
Furthermore, on the right side, one should paint an image of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva;
on the left side, one should paint an image of Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva.
Each should hold their respective insignia according to their original ordinances.
Outside the palace,
on the right side within the ocean, one should paint the Nāga King Nanda.
On his crown he possesses nine heads and rides upon black clouds;
in his left hand he holds a precious jewel,
guarding the King of Wish-fulfilling Jewels.
In the ocean on the left side, depict the Nāga King Bhadrananda,
with seven heads upon his crown, riding atop black clouds,
and holding a maṇi jewel in his right hand.
One should protect and uphold the image of the King of Maṇi Jewels;
this is called the ritual of the painted image maṇḍala.
One should then form mudrās and perform recitation while facing this very image.
The Unsurpassed, Most Profound, and Secret Dharma, incomparable and peerless, wherein immeasurable *siddhis* are spontaneously attained without seeking.
The Great Maṇḍala Image Diagram, Part 5: Chapter Five on the Consecration Seals and Mantras. At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajraguhyapāṇi, saying:
If there is a son of the Buddha who wishes to attain the supreme *mahāsiddhi* dharma,
he must follow the instructions of the Great Master;
it is not within the scope of his own wisdom.
First receive the empowerment ritual;
thereafter, bind the seal of the King of Wish-Fulfilling Jewels and recite the root dhāraṇī.
"I now wish to speak; would you like to hear it?
The Bodhisattva Guhyapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying, "May the Buddha, the World-Honored One, speak for us."
"I wish to hear it with joy.
Thereupon, the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
spoke the root dhāraṇī, saying:
Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Tadyathā. Oṃ amogha-maṇi mahāmaṇi padmamaṇi svāhā. After the Buddha had spoken this dhāraṇī, [he said:]...
Immediately, the dragon palace shook in six ways,
and wish-fulfilling jewels rained down,
like the heavy downpour of spring rain.
At that time, the great assembly all attained realization of the fruits [of the path].
The Dragon King’s daughter, the virtuous woman, gave rise to the great bodhicitta and also made this vow:

"May I protect wherever the Tathāgata’s bequeathed teachings and his physical remains reside, as well as whatever kingdoms contain the king of wish-fulfilling jewels spoken of by the Buddha among men."
Just as one protects one's own life and guards one's own clothing,
so too shall you increase the majesty of the jewel so that siddhi may be attained without deficiency.
Simply request my presence to protect the precious gem.
He excavated a precious pond and planted lotus flowers therein; neither humans nor animals were seen there,
for only the Ācārya and his attendant were permitted to enter.
"No others shall enter.
I dwell within this place to guard the precious jewel and to protect and uphold the True Dharma."
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent!
O Water-Goddess, daughter of the Great Dragon King Sūvarṇaprabhāsa,
it shall be as you have wished."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Guhyapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying,
"I only pray that you will explain this Great Dhāraṇī of the Great Consecration Seal.
The Buddha said to the Bodhisattva Guhyapāṇi:
This is the secret seal of the very heart of all Tathāgatas.

The *Sūtra of the Secret Manifestation of Buddhahood through the Cakravartin Wish-Fulfilling Jewel Mantra-King*:
This sūtra is traditionally said to have been transmitted from the Great Master Goso Hōshō Kongō Shin’ya Sōjō.
From the present down to our late master, the Sōjō of Hannyaji,
there have been twelve generations since Mahāvairocana Tathāgata;
this direct line of succession consists of but a single person at each stage.
It was subsequently transmitted by Fuyou,
who kept it as a secret as if it were his own eyes.
Now, the Great Dharma Master Yuangao has been granted it.
On the twenty-third day of the eighth month of the third year of Tenryaku (1389), the year of Jia-you, the Junior Acharya,
Imperial Attendant, and Chief Zen Master Jun’yu was conferred as the Acharya.
